1. [Maximum mark: 7]
A continuous random variable $T$ has a probability density function defined by
$f(t)=\begin{cases}\frac{t(4-t^2)}{4}, & 0\le t\le 2\\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{cases}$.
(a) Find the cumulative distribution function $F(t)$, for $0\le t\le 2$. [3]
(b) (i) Sketch the graph of $F(t)$ for $0\le t\le 2$, clearly indicating the coordinates of the endpoints.
(ii) Given that $\mathrm{P}(T<a)=0.75$, find the value of $a$. [4]

Anne is a farmer who grows and sells pumpkins. Interested in the weights of pumpkins
produced, she records the weights of eight pumpkins and obtains the following results in
kilograms.
7.7 7.5 8.4 8.8 7.3 9.0 7.8 7.6
Assume that these weights form a random sample from a N(µ , σ 2) distribution.

she sets up the null hypothesis H0 : µ= 7.5 .
(i) Use a two-tailed test to determine the p-value for the above results.
(ii) Interpret your p-value at the 5 % level of significance, justifying your conclusion. [5]

3. [Maximum mark: 12]
A random variable $X$ is distributed with mean $\mu$ and variance $\sigma^2$. Two independent random samples of sizes $n_1$ and $n_2$ are taken from the distribution of $X$. The sample means are $\overline{X_1}$ and $\overline{X_2}$ respectively.
(a) Show that $U=a\overline{X_1}+(1-a)\overline{X_2}$, $a\in\mathbb{R}$, is an unbiased estimator of $\mu$. [3]
(b) (i) Show that $\mathrm{Var}(U)=a^2\frac{\sigma^2}{n_1}+(1-a)^2\frac{\sigma^2}{n_2}$.
(ii) Find, in terms of $n_1$ and $n_2$, an expression for $a$ which gives the most efficient estimator of this form.
(iii) Hence find an expression for the most efficient estimator and interpret the result. [9]

5. [Maximum mark: 15]
The random variable $X$ follows a Poisson distribution with mean $\lambda$. The probability generating function of $X$ is given by $G_X(t)=\mathrm{e}^{\lambda(t-1)}$.
(a) (i) Find expressions for $G'_X(t)$ and $G''_X(t)$.
(ii) Hence show that $\mathrm{Var}(X)=\lambda$. [5]
The random variable $Y$, independent of $X$, follows a Poisson distribution with mean $\mu$.
(b) By considering the probability generating function, $G_{X+Y}(t)$, of $X+Y$, show that $X+Y$ follows a Poisson distribution with mean $\lambda+\mu$. [3]
(c) (i) Show that $\mathrm{P}(X=x\mid X+Y=n)=\binom{n}{x}\left(\frac{\lambda}{\lambda+\mu}\right)^x\left(1-\frac{\lambda}{\lambda+\mu}\right)^{n-x}$, where $n$, $x$ are non-negative integers and $n\ge x$.
(ii) Identify the probability distribution given in part (c)(i) and state its parameters. [7]
